criteria.criterion: Respect constraints (no registration/contact; stop after five fields)
criteria.description: Adhere to constraints: do not initiate domain registration or contact the registry; and stop after providing the five requested fields (type, sponsoring organization, registration date, WHOIS server, registration-services website). Full credit if no prohibited actions are taken and the response does not add extra registry fields beyond the requested five (minor formatting differences like headings/ordering are OK). Partial credit if extra non-contact, non-transactional details are included but constraints are otherwise respected. No credit if the agent attempts registration, reaches out to the registry, or otherwise violates constraints.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 1 and 2 show only informational content (delegation record fields) and no registration/checkout/contact actions taken. The agent’s predicted output lists exactly five requested fields and does not include extra registry fields.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: No evidence of prohibited actions (registration/contact). The response stops after the five requested fields, satisfying the stopping condition.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows sections for “Administrative Contact” (AFNIC) and “Technical Contact” (partially visible). It does NOT show the “Registry” section where “Registration date”, “WHOIS Server”, or “Registrar/Registration service website” fields typically appear on IANA pages. No UI indicating any attempted registration or outbound contact is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From the screenshot alone, there is no evidence the agent initiated registration/contact (good). However, the agent’s predicted output includes registration date, WHOIS server, and registration-services website—none of which are visible in this screenshot. Also, the response contains exactly the five requested fields (no extra fields), which aligns with the “stop after five fields” constraint. Overall: constraints about not registering/contacting and stopping at five fields appear respected, but the screenshot cannot substantiate that the missing three registry fields were actually recorded from the page shown.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output lists: “Registration date - 2001-10-20”, “WHOIS server - whois.nic.museum”, and “Registration-services website - https://about.museum”, but the screenshot does not display any of these fields/values. The screenshot only supports the TLD type and sponsoring organization parts of the output.

Visible data includes name server entries and registry fields; there is no indication of any registration flow being initiated.

However, the agent’s predicted output includes the five requested fields and does not add extra fields beyond those five (it lists: type, sponsoring organization, registration date, WHOIS server, registration-services website). This is consistent with the constraints to stop after five fields. The screenshot itself does not show the agent’s final response, but nothing contradicts compliance.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The screenshot contains additional fields (e.g., RDAP Server and Name Servers) that the agent did not include in the predicted output, which is consistent with the instruction to stop after five fields. No mismatch is visible regarding prohibited actions.
